sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text: Bassens, a port and industrial commune on the right bank of the Garonne in Gironde, has no parking policy of its own that we could find; what applies comes from Bordeaux Métropole. The municipal page says the town is served by tram line A, whose terminus is La Gardette-Bassens-Carbon-Blanc, by six bus lines and by a park-and-ride at La Gardette, and that Liane 7 runs every 12 to 15 minutes in the day [13]. The Métropole's low-emission zone has applied inside the ring road since 1 January 2025; unclassified vehicles may use 11 listed park-and-rides via dedicated access roads, which include Buttinière and Lauriers in Lormont but not La Gardette, and the page does not say whether Bassens is inside the zone [7]. We found no municipal paid-zone, blue-zone or resident-permit rules. The port and industrial zone covers 600 hectares, 60% of the territory, with about 4,000 direct jobs, which the page does not link to parking [14].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text: The development is at the station and in the park-and-ride fares. The Bassens station interchange was inaugurated on 24 June 2025 after works begun in May 2024, with 68 car spaces, a secure bike park and a redesigned avenue, costing 2.48 million euros; the station has 41 trains a day, and a Presqu'île/Campus express bus is planned to serve Bassens by 2027 [8]. Under the Keolis concession, five dynamic signs showing free park-and-ride spaces were installed, one of them on Avenue Raoul Bourdieu in Bassens, and the Métropole voted a new offer on 29 September 2023 allowing short stays of two to five days at some park-and-rides, including La Gardette Nord and Sud [5]. A local news site reported on 29 September 2026 that the Métropole plans an average 3% rise in TBM fares for 2027, including the park-and-ride ticket going from 4.50 to 5 euros; this is a plan before council approval and not confirmed in an official text [12]. A secure bike box opposite the town hall serves up to six bikes [15]. The La Gardette list shows no charging spaces [11].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
TBM runs 28 park-and-rides across the Métropole [6]. At La Gardette it lists two car parks on Avenue des Griffons: one open to all with 242 spaces and one for season-ticket holders with 151 [0]. Same-day parking is included in a TBM subscription; others pay 4.50 euros, or 3.50 at La Gardette Nord and Sud, for a ticket giving seven round trips for one to seven people [1]. Short stays of two to five days cost 12, 15, 20 and 25 euros [2]. TBM's pages disagree on closing hours and on the fine for staying outside them, 15 or 25 euros, so we do not state either [4].

Our data label three car parks as Bassens, with 900 spaces, but two of them, Buttinière (600 spaces) and Lauriers (149), are in Lormont according to the Métropole's low-emission zone page, so only La Gardette Sud (151) is certainly in the commune. Measured since 24 September 2026, occupancy averaged about 31% on weekdays and 8% at weekends, weighted by spaces, which is a commuter pattern. Buttinière averaged 40% on weekdays and reached 99% on a Thursday around midday, Lauriers 16%, and La Gardette Sud only 9%. About four weeks of data.
